# Volume 4 — CHAPTER 25 THE WRITING OF THE BOOK

!!! note "Source text"
    Passages cited on the wiki pages link into this page. Only volumes at or before
    this page's cutoff are present.

The following morning, Adrian Treleaven arrived at the small dwelling, intensely thrilled. “Mrs. Carrow, a truly marvellous book—it is completely marvellous. Should I be allowed to possess it and draw upon its contents for a work, I am convinced I could create the most outstanding novel of the year from it. Is it likely Captain Saul would permit me to perform this?”
{: #nw-v04-c25-p0000 }

“Allow you! I am certain he would be thrilled,” Nell exclaimed. “I confess that this was precisely my intention when I brought you below yesterday evening. Captain Saul has constantly desired to find someone who could compose his life-book correctly for him.”
{: #nw-v04-c25-p0001 }

“Would you accompany me to the Point tonight, Mrs. Carrow? I will personally inquire of him regarding that life-book, yet I desire that you inform him that the tale of lost Margaret was imparted to me by you, and inquire whether he would permit me to employ it as a romantic thread to interweave the life-book’s stories into a unified whole.”
{: #nw-v04-c25-p0002 }

Adrian Treleaven’s revelation of his proposal made Captain Saul feel unprecedentedly thrilled. His long-held ambition would finally come to fruition, allowing his “life-book” to be presented to the public. Additionally, he felt delighted about incorporating the tale of the vanished Margaret into its pages.
{: #nw-v04-c25-p0003 }

“Her name won't be forgotten because of it,” he murmured with longing.
{: #nw-v04-c25-p0004 }

“It’s for that reason I desire to have it inserted.”
{: #nw-v04-c25-p0005 }

“We shall work together,” Adrian exclaimed with joy. “The soul will be provided by you and the body by me. Oh, Captain Saul, a renowned book will be authored by the two of us. And our labor will commence immediately.”
{: #nw-v04-c25-p0006 }

“And to imagine that the schoolmaster’s grandson is going to write my book!” Captain Saul cried out. “Boy, I held your grandfather as my closest companion. To my mind, he was without equal. Now I understand the reason for my lengthy wait. The writing had to hold off until the proper person arrived. You BELONG in this place—the spirit of this ancient north shore resides within you—you are the sole person who COULD write it.”
{: #nw-v04-c25-p0007 }

They agreed to assign the small chamber adjoining the lighthouse's living room to Adrian as a workroom. Because Adrian lacked knowledge regarding numerous aspects of maritime and gulf traditions, it was essential for Captain Saul to remain close by while he composed to provide advice.
{: #nw-v04-c25-p0008 }

Work on the volume commenced for him on the following morning, a task to which he devoted his entire being. Regarding Captain Saul, the summer brought him great joy. The small chamber where Adrian laboured was viewed by him as a holy place. While Adrian discussed every detail with Captain Saul, the written pages were kept hidden from his sight.
{: #nw-v04-c25-p0009 }

“It is necessary for you to hold off until publication,” he remarked. “After that, you will receive everything together in its finest condition.”
{: #nw-v04-c25-p0010 }

He drew unreservedly from the riches of his personal history. He pondered and fantasised about the departed Margaret to the point where she gained a vibrant presence for him and inhabited his writing. With the book’s advancement, it completely consumed him, driving him to labor upon it with intense excitement. He permitted Nell and Lorna to peruse the text and offer feedback; furthermore, the final chapter of the volume, which reviewers subsequently saw fit to label idyllic, was based on an idea provided by Lorna.
{: #nw-v04-c25-p0011 }

Nell wrapped her arms around herself in sheer joy because her scheme had worked so well.
{: #nw-v04-c25-p0012 }

“The moment I set eyes on Adrian Treleaven, I realized he was the ideal person for the task,” she remarked to Hugh. “His countenance revealed both humor and passion, which, combined with his skill for expression, provided precisely what was required to write a book of that nature. In the words of Mrs. Agatha, he was foreordained for the role.”
{: #nw-v04-c25-p0013 }

Adrian Treleaven engaged in writing during the morning hours. The afternoon period was usually occupied by a cheerful excursion alongside the Carrows. Lorna frequently joined them as well, because Captain Saul regularly assumed responsibility for Rufus so that she could be liberated. They navigated boats across the harbor and along the trio of lovely rivers that emptied into it; they held clambakes upon the bar as well as mussel-bakes over the rocks; they gathered strawberries among the sand-dunes; they embarked on cod-fishing trips accompanied by Captain Saul; they targeted plover within the coastal pastures and wild ducks inside the cove—or rather, the male members of the party did. During the evening hours they wandered through the low-lying, daisied, coastal pastures beneath a golden moon, or else they gathered inside the living room of the small house where the chill of the ocean wind frequently made a driftwood fire welcome, discussing the endless topics that joyful, enthusiastic, intelligent youth are capable of discovering to converse about.
{: #nw-v04-c25-p0014 }

From the exact date she had confessed to Nell, Lorna had transformed into a completely different person. Not a hint remained of her former distance and reticence, nor any trace of her previous rancor. The youth she had been denied appeared to return to her alongside her mature womanhood; she opened up like a blossom of fire and fragrance; during the twilight gatherings of that magical summer, no one laughed more easily or possessed a sharper wit than she did. Whenever she was absent, everyone sensed that their time together was missing a delightful essence. Her inner soul had awakened, illuminating her beauty in the manner of a rose-colored light glowing through a perfect alabaster urn. At times, the sheer brilliance of her presence seemed to make Nell’s eyes throb. Regarding Adrian Treleaven, the "Margaret" in his manuscript—despite possessing the gentle brown locks and pixie-like features of the actual young woman who had disappeared such a long time back, "pillowed where lost Atlantis sleeps"—carried the character of Lorna Vane, just as it unfolded before him throughout those blissful times at Seven Gulls Harbor.
{: #nw-v04-c25-p0015 }

Taken as a whole, it proved to be an unforgettably grand summer—the sort of season that rarely occurs in anyone's existence, yet bequeaths a wealth of lovely recollections upon its departure—a summer that, through a happy blending of pleasant weather, pleasant companions, and pleasant activities, approaches perfection as closely as anything possibly can in this life.
{: #nw-v04-c25-p0016 }

“It’s too good to endure,” Nell remarked softly to herself, uttering a small sigh, on that day in September when a particular chill in the breeze and a particular hue of vivid blue across the gulf water indicated that autumn was right at hand.
{: #nw-v04-c25-p0017 }

That night, Adrian Treleaven informed them that his book was completed and his holiday had to conclude.
{: #nw-v04-c25-p0018 }

“There is still quite a lot of work for me to perform on it—editing, trimming, and the like,” he remarked, “however, it is essentially finished. The final line was composed by me earlier today. Should I manage to locate a publisher, its release will likely occur during the upcoming summer or autumn.”
{: #nw-v04-c25-p0019 }

Adrian felt fairly certain about securing a publisher. It was clear to him that his creation was a great book—one destined for remarkable success—a work that would endure. He was aware of the fame and fortune it would earn him; yet, upon finishing its final line, he rested his head against the manuscript and remained in that position for a while. Nor were his reflections centered on the fine accomplishment he had achieved.
{: #nw-v04-c25-p0020 }
